records.supported_name_scope: La Mana and Fleuve Mana are source wordings for the representative main-river corridor. The selected short western tributary is a lower Arouani approach, not an alias or extension of the Mana name. Regional cartography bridges the upper-middle connection between the more detailed source sheets; the coastal endpoint remains a generalized approach rather than a precise present-day mouth.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This is the interior Mana river east of the Maroni, not the Maroni border river, the Sinnamary farther east, the separate Arouani tributary, or the coastal Acarouany waterway. French territorial administration does not place this geographic object in Europe.
records.region: Western French Guiana, South America; Saül headwater region northward through the interior Mana corridor to Mana bourg and the coastal approach.
records.completion_scope: All four modeled mainstem stage features, comprising 166 modeled line pieces, and the one tributary stage feature, comprising three short pieces, were considered as one generalized selection. Readable Saül, Trinité, municipal and Bon Espoir cartography supports the upper, middle, lower and tributary routes. The retained whole-Guyane drainage map unambiguously bridges the short upper-middle interval at a coarser regional naming scale. Complete representative correspondence does not imply equal detail everywhere, a name for every minor feeder, or present-day shoreline precision.

naming_scope_details.representative_name: La Mana / Fleuve Mana, bounded to the supported main-river corridor; no formal alias registry is asserted.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Saül–Mont Galbao headwater setting and the northward upper Mana connection are supported by readable topographic cartography. A short sheet-edge interval is bridged by the retained park drainage map at coarser regional naming scale.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Only a lower Arouani approach is selected. Arouani remains a separate component name. No additional names are invented for minor feeders or unselected upstream branches.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Coastal approach northwest of Mana bourg. Complete estuary, modern mouth, shoreline and administrative limit are outside the supported terminal claim.
naming_scope_details.source_scope: Municipal report reflects modifications through February 2018 but includes older topographic and planning inputs. Bon Espoir report is October 2016. ZNIEFF map sheets are cartographed March 2013 and distributed in the official 2014 inventory update. These dates describe source editions, not current environmental, mining or navigation conditions.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The rendered mainstem length is a property of the generalized selection, not an official river length. MAIN_RIV membership and stage segmentation do not authorize one scalar name for every piece. No Korean name is inferred.
naming_scope_details.remaining_work: No further source acquisition is required for this bounded representative-name finding. Scalar or automatic application remains disabled. A more precise shoreline exercise is outside the present task.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: A southern interior beginning, long northward western leg, broad northeastward turn followed by an irregular eastward course and southeastward terminal approach toward the southeastern glaciated margin. Nearby coastal names are regional anchors only; the exact terminal natural feature is unassigned.
records.region: Southeastern Greenland Inland Ice and eastern glaciated margin, broadly inland of the Køge Bugt coastal region.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: No whole-route natural river candidate; terminal glacier/fjord/stream identity remains unassigned.

records.supported_name_scope: The complete selection combines an Orlando urban lake and controlled-outlet approach, Boggy Creek, the East Tohopekaliga–Tohopekaliga–Cypress–Hatchineha–Kissimmee lake/canal chain, Kissimmee River/C-38, a modeled Lake Okeechobee crossing, and the Moore Haven–Hicpochee–Caloosahatchee/C-43 continuation.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The northern approach is within the Boggy Creek urban-lake corridor east of Shingle Creek. The selection uses East Lake Tohopekaliga and then the westward canal connection, rather than naming the adjacent Shingle Creek or eastern Hart/Alligator/Gentry routes as selected tributaries. At Lake Okeechobee it turns toward Moore Haven and Caloosahatchee, not east along St. Lucie or south into the Everglades canals. The western endpoint lies beyond the Franklin/Olga setting but upstream of central Fort Myers and does not reach the Gulf.
records.region: Central and southwestern Florida, United States
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative correspondence and naming-scope assessment of both selected fragments. Readable primary cartography covers the urban northern approach, lake chain, lower Kissimmee, Okeechobee transition and complete western river corridor. The hold reflects multiple named waterways, separate lakes, engineered outlets/canals and generalized lake-routing geometry, rather than a substantial missing-map gap. Follow-up is required before any whole-group label, reach subdivision or name application. Detailed assignment of every urban drain, lake vertex or historical versus restored channel is intentionally not claimed.

naming_scope_details.whole_group_scope: Two mainstem-role fragments combine distinct rivers/creek, several separate lakes and engineered conveyances. No supported single whole-group hydronym was established.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: There are no selected tributary-role fragments. Nearby named tributaries and lake branches provide disambiguation only; none is silently incorporated into this selection.
naming_scope_details.headwater_scope: Urban lakes and controlled/overflow drainage in the Boggy Creek basin. The beginning is a modeled start, not an official source. Holden’s landlocked/drainwell status cautions against reading model connectivity as permanent surface flow.
naming_scope_details.lake_chain_scope: East Lake Tohopekaliga, Lake Tohopekaliga, Cypress Lake, Lake Hatchineha and Lake Kissimmee remain separate waterbody names. C-31, C-35, C-36 and C-37 are component canal labels; no lake name is proposed as a river alias.
naming_scope_details.kissimmee_scope: Kissimmee River/C-38 is supported for the lower river corridor between Lake Kissimmee and Lake Okeechobee. The historical map does not adjudicate every model vertex against present restoration routing.
naming_scope_details.okeechobee_scope: Lake Okeechobee and its western-margin/outlet connection are positive mapped components. The generalized interior route lacks a separate verified channel identity and is not forced into a rim-canal or natural-river name.
naming_scope_details.caloosahatchee_scope: Caloosahatchee River/C-43 is supported westward from the Moore Haven/Hicpochee connection through the main engineered-river corridor. The remaining lower selected portion ends upstream of Fort Myers and the complete estuary.
naming_scope_details.historical_and_flow_scope: All engineering and restoration descriptions are date-bounded source accounts. No present flow direction, perennial continuity, lock availability, current gate operations, exact shoreline, flood boundary or modern restoration completion is asserted.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: Agency and county cartography establishes named geographic components and their relationships. Basin/planning-area names, recreation routes and infrastructure IDs do not independently confer one hydronym on the entire model group.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 358.362 km rendered length is a model length, not an official river length. Mainstem role and stage attributes do not define name boundaries. No Korean form, formal naming act or whole-group scalar is established.
naming_scope_details.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative correspondence and naming-scope assessment of both selected fragments. Readable primary cartography covers the urban northern approach, lake chain, lower Kissimmee, Okeechobee transition and complete western river corridor. The hold reflects multiple named waterways, separate lakes, engineered outlets/canals and generalized lake-routing geometry, rather than a substantial missing-map gap. Follow-up is required before any whole-group label, reach subdivision or name application. Detailed assignment of every urban drain, lake vertex or historical versus restored channel is intentionally not claimed.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Tocuyo identifies the representative receiving river and its middle-to-lower coastward corridor. The selected western beginning belongs to the El Ermitaño reservoir/tributary approach and continues through the Morere valley. These component reaches are not all assigned the Tocuyo name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route enters the Tocuyo through its western tributary system. It is not the southern Andean upper Tocuyo through El Tocuyo, Dos Cerritos and Atarigua, and is not the adjacent Aroa or Yaracuy drainage.
records.region: Northwestern Venezuela, from the western Torres/Carora drainage in Lara through the middle Tocuyo corridor toward the Caribbean coastal plain of Falcón.
records.completion_scope: The single generalized selected path was considered from its western beginning, through the reservoir-side approach and Carora–Aregue–Río Tocuyo connection, to its middle and lower coastward corridor. Independent acquired maps support this whole regional connection. Small unnamed connectors, exact upper name transitions and the present shoreline are outside the naming conclusion.

naming_scope_details.representative_name: Río Tocuyo is a representative system identity, not a claim that the full modeled longest route has one name.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: El Ermitaño reservoir/tributary setting and its connected western approach to Carora. The 2007 study discusses Diquiva and Morere subbasins, but the acquired maps do not securely establish every reach-level name transition; Diquiva is not accepted as a uniform label for this whole approach.
naming_scope_details.middle_scope: The MOP map supports Morere for the Carora–Aregue valley and its receiving Tocuyo connection. Downstream the whole-basin map supports the Tocuyo corridor through the middle and lower basin.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower river/coastal approach only. No precise tidal boundary, mouth closure, coastal channel split or shoreline date is asserted.
naming_scope_details.source_scope: Historical sources are used for regional geographic correspondence and printed naming only. Reservoir operating status, current water conditions and present administrative boundaries are not inferred.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The rendered mainstem and system grouping are modeled selections, not an official river length, official source point or permission to rename every tributary. Korean wording remains unassigned.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
